meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.
Yesterday we opened the shop early.

acabar.gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)

meanings.en: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
meanings.note: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something'.

examples.trans: I have just arrived from the market.

examples.text: Ya acabamos el trabajo de hoy.
examples.trans: We already finished today's work.

meanings.note: Feminine noun that takes el in the singular before stressed initial /a/ (el agua fría).

examples.text: Quiero un vaso de agua fría.
examples.trans: I want a glass of cold water.

examples.text: El agua de la ducha sale caliente.
examples.trans: The shower water comes out hot.

meanings.note: Al aire libre means 'outdoors'.

examples.text: El aire es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The air is very important here.
We talk about the air.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Placed after a noun, means 'historic' or 'old-fashioned'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.

examples.text: Encantada, Tomás, ¡siempre que nadie hable de vender pianos antiguos!
examples.trans: Gladly, Tomas, as long as nobody talks about selling old pianos!

meanings.note: Air or water bubble.

examples.trans: The bubble is here.

examples.text: Vemos las burbujas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bubbles from the door.

meanings.note: Caja de herramientas = toolbox; la caja also means the cash register/box.

examples.trans: The box is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cajas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the boxs from the door.

meanings.note: Heating and hot-water boiler.

examples.trans: The boiler is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the boilers from the door.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

meanings.note: Tener calor = to feel hot; hacer calor = to be warm weather.

examples.text: El calor es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The heat is very important here.
We talk about the heat.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?
Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Con desayuno incluido = with breakfast included.

examples.trans: The breakfast is here.

examples.text: Vemos los desayunos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the breakfasts from the door.

meanings.note: Literally 'waker-upper', from despertar.

examples.trans: The alarm clock is here.

examples.text: Vemos los despertadores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the alarm clocks from the door.

meanings.note: Darse una ducha = to take a shower.

examples.trans: The shower is here.

examples.text: Vemos las duchas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the showers from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

meanings.note: Neuter pronoun; por eso = that is why.

examples.trans: That is why I brought two umbrellas.
What does that mean exactly?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.note: Built from hierro/ferro (iron).

examples.trans: The hardware shop is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ferreterías desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hardware shops from the door.

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el frío), means 'the cold'.

examples.trans: It is a cold piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

ganar.gloss: to win; to beat (ganar a); to earn

meanings.en: to win; to beat (ganar a); to earn
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Esta vista gana a cualquier postal.
examples.trans: This view beats any postcard.
With patience we always save time.

guardar.gloss: to keep; to put away; to guard

meanings.en: to keep; to put away; to guard
meanings.note: Everyday verb for putting something safely away in a pocket or cupboard.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en este cajón.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in this drawer.

examples.text: Te guardé el último rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I saved the last cinnamon roll for you.

meanings.note: La guía de viajes = the travel guidebook.

examples.trans: The guidebook is here.

examples.text: Vemos las guías desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the guidebooks from the door.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: As a noun (el helado), means 'ice cream'.

examples.trans: It is a freezing piece.

examples.text: Mañana a las siete de la mañana, el agua de la ducha va a salir helada.
examples.trans: Tomorrow at seven in the morning, the shower water is going to come out ice-cold.

meanings.note: Caja de herramientas = toolbox.

examples.trans: The tool is here.

examples.text: Vemos las herramientas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tools from the door.

meanings.note: ¿Qué hora es? asks the clock time.

examples.trans: The hour is here.

examples.text: Vemos las horas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hours from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine: la inspectora.

examples.trans: The inspector is here.

examples.text: Vemos los inspectores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the inspectors from the door.

meanings.note: Coldest season of the year.

examples.trans: The winter is here.

examples.text: Vemos los inviernos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the winters from the door.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.
How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: De ladrillo = made of brick.

examples.trans: The brick is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ladrillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bricks from the door.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Yellow copper-zinc alloy used for keys, lamps, and valves.

examples.text: El latón es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The brass is very important here.
We talk about the brass.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Nada mal = not bad at all; menos mal = thank goodness.

examples.text: Nada mal para el primer día.
examples.trans: Not bad at all for the first day.
Thank goodness you brought an umbrella!

meanings.note: Shortens to mal before masculine singular nouns (mal tiempo); malas noticias = bad news.

examples.trans: It is a bad piece.
Bad news

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.
examples.trans: In the morning we serve hot coffee.
See you tomorrow at eight!

meanings.note: Exact measurement or step.

examples.trans: The measurement is here.

examples.text: Vemos las medidas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the measurements from the door.

meanings.note: Media vuelta = half-turn (turn around); medio vaso = half a glass.

examples.trans: It is a half piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Por lo menos = at least; echar de menos = to miss; a menos que = unless.

examples.trans: It is ten to eight.

examples.text: Por lo menos ya no llueve.
examples.trans: At least it is no longer raining.

meanings.note: Exterior or structural masonry wall.

examples.trans: The thick wall is here.

examples.text: Vemos los muros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the thick walls from the door.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Buena noticia! = Good news!

examples.trans: The piece of news is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noticias desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the piece of newss from the door.

meanings.note: Becomes u before words starting with o- or ho-.

examples.trans: Do you prefer coffee or hot tea?
Do we open today or wait until tomorrow?

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.note: Hermano pequeño = younger brother; de pequeño = as a child.

examples.trans: It is a small piece.

examples.text: Hay una pequeña tarjeta de cartón atada al asa.
examples.trans: There is a small cardboard card tied to the handle.

meanings.note: Planta baja = ground floor; primera planta = first floor; also a green plant.

examples.trans: The floor / storey is here.

examples.text: Vemos las plantas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the floor / storeys from the door.

poner.gloss: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)

meanings.en: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)
meanings.note: Irregular: pongo, pon, puse, puesto; ponerse nervioso = get nervous.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas limpias en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two clean cups on the table.

examples.text: Pon la maleta junto al mostrador.
examples.trans: Set the suitcase beside the counter.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: One word without accent (distinct from ¿por qué? = why?).

examples.text: Abro la ventana porque hace calor.
examples.trans: I open the window because it is warm.
She smiles because it smells of cinnamon.

meanings.note: Water or boiler pressure.

examples.text: La presión es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The pressure is very important here.
We talk about the pressure.

meanings.note: Masculine noun in Spanish: el puente de piedra.

examples.trans: The bridge is here.

examples.text: Vemos los puentes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bridges from the door.

punto.gloss: dot; point (en punto = on the dot; a punto de = about to)

meanings.en: dot; point (en punto = on the dot; a punto de = about to)
meanings.note: A las nueve en punto = at nine o'clock sharp.

examples.trans: The dot is here.

examples.text: Vemos los puntos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the dots from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Hot-water room radiator.

examples.trans: The radiator is here.

examples.text: Vemos los radiadores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the radiators from the door.

meanings.note: Una válvula de repuesto = a spare valve.

examples.trans: The spare part is here.

examples.text: Vemos los repuestos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the spare parts from the door.

meanings.note: Regular verb with irregular past participle roto.

examples.text: Ten cuidado de no romper la taza.
examples.trans: Be careful not to break the cup.

examples.text: El viento rompió una rama seca.
examples.trans: The wind snapped a dry branch.

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.
I leave early for the station.

seguir.gloss: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)

meanings.en: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sigo, sigue, siguió); seguir + gerund = keep doing.

examples.text: Sigue todo recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the bridge.
Is the water still hot?

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Las siete y cuarto = seven fifteen.

examples.text: La habitación siete mira al patio.
examples.trans: Room seven overlooks the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las siete y media.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at seven thirty.

meanings.note: ¿Qué significa eso? = What does that mean?

examples.trans: What does this old word mean?

examples.text: Dos toques significan que llaman arriba.
examples.trans: Two rings mean someone is calling upstairs.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

meanings.note: Negative counterpart of también.

examples.text: Tampoco hay espejo en la pared.
examples.trans: There is no mirror on the wall either.
'I am in no rush.' 'Me neither.'

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Shortens to tercer before masculine singular nouns (el tercer escalón).

examples.trans: It is a third piece.
Come on, race you to the third floor!

meanings.note: Unaccented possessive (tu llave / tus llaves), distinct from accented pronoun tú.

examples.trans: Where is your toolbox?
I recognized your handwriting right away.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Uso gafas solo para leer letra pequeña.
examples.trans: I wear glasses only for reading fine print.
We use fresh lemons from the courtyard.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: En ese puesto venden flores frescas.
examples.trans: At that stall they sell fresh flowers.

examples.text: Vendieron la casa familiar hace tres años.
examples.trans: They sold the family house three years ago.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Válvula de latón = brass valve.

examples.trans: The valve is here.

examples.text: Vemos las válvulas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the valves from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Carries a written accent on ú.

examples.trans: It is a last piece.

examples.text: Diez, once, doce. Exacto hasta la última moneda. ¡Gracias!
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last coin. Thank you!
